title: Genuine cross-frequency coupling networks in human resting-state electrophysiological recordings (Siebenhuehner et al., 2020): SEEG and MEG connectomes (derivative)
description: A derivative repackaging of the public Dryad release accompanying Siebenhühner et al. (2020). It provides per-subject connectivity matrices computed from 10-minute resting-state SEEG (59 epilepsy patients) and MEG (19 healthy participants, plus a 10-participant eyes-open/eyes-closed cohort). Measures include phase synchrony (PLV, wPLI), cross-frequency phase synchrony, phase-amplitude coupling and amplitude-envelope coupling, each with surrogate values. Supporting parcel and contact files, neuropsychological scores and the plotted values of the article's figures are also included. Raw recordings are not available.
methods_description: SEEG was recorded for 10 min eyes-closed at 1000 Hz (192 channels) in 59 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Contacts were localized with CT and assigned to the 148-parcel Destrieux atlas, and closest-white-matter referencing was applied. MEG was recorded for 10 min eyes-open with a 306-channel Elekta/MEGIN system, processed with tSSS and ICA, and source-modelled with MNE onto 200 parcels with fidelity weighting. Morlet wavelet filter banks (m=5, up to 315 Hz) were used to compute synchrony and coupling matrices with surrogate values.
